utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise. I really don't want to interrupt my colleague. But I was just informed by Mr. Zaric that he hasn't received his medicine that he usually does, and I'm afraid that this is what caused problems with Mr. Zaric a couple -- two days ago, when he didn't receive this medicine, he suffered these pains and everything. So I just asked the guards whether they brought this for Mr. Zaric. They brought just one of his medicine, not the other one. So Mr. Zaric asked me to -- this issue just to inform the Trial Chamber that the possibility of some problems may occur, because this is what happened two days ago, and he actually collapsed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The position is that the medicine is available but it hasn't yet been brought?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He -- well, I was informed by the guards that they just have one, one pill, that Mr. Zaric usually does take, but the other one they didn't get from the Detention Unit. They didn't get it for Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So that's the problem that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber requests the Registrar's Office to look into the matter right away and keep us informed, as we have to go on with the witnesses who are already here. I do hope that the medicine gets sent right away. We can proceed. Is the Prosecution cross-examining?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Before I begin, there's just one very brief matter in relation to the 92 bis statements. On Monday, Your Honours asked us to file a response by Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We actually filed it this morning, being Thursday, and I apologise for that. The reason was Mr. Di Fazio was sick on Monday, and I realised yesterday when we were doing it we had to file two, a confidential and a publicly redacted version because of something referred to in one of them which took longer than anticipated and I didn't have a chance to speak to the Registry -- sorry to the legal officer or have it filed by 5.00 yesterday. So we filed it at 9.00 and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Then it will be considered validly filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sarkanovic. I want to continue from where we were yesterday --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- firstly by -- I just want you to clarify something which, having looked at the transcript overnight, isn't completely clear. That was yesterday afternoon I was asking you about your investigations and the statements you took and the law which you were personally applying. Now, you worked in the -- you worked as part of your war assignment, in the SUP for almost two months. Yesterday you said that it was the Penal Code. What I'm trying to clarify, which wasn't clear from the transcript yesterday, was which precise part of the Penal Code, what was the name of the offence that you were investigating and taking statements in relation to, the name of the offence and, if you can remember, the section of the code.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my work at that time in the SUP, I used the Law on Criminal Procedure and the Criminal Code, or the Penal Code, which had been adopted from the former Yugoslavia. According to the Law on Criminal Procedure, I conducted interviews. This is under this law, that there was a provision in relation to criminal offences that provided for by the Penal Code and this is to do with the armed rebellion and illegal possession of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The armed rebellion you just referred to, is that an offence of insurrection against a state?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the offences you were investigating in April, May, and June 1992 were insurrection against a state; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which state was that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the insurrection against the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina you're investigating in those three different months I referred to was insurrection by Muslims and Croats against the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering that they were arming themselves legally [as interpreted], that's how it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one correction for the transcript. Line -- page 4, line 5. It should read illegally instead of legally. That is what the witness said, otherwise it has no sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Sarkanovic, I just want to correct that. The transcript says legally. You in fact said illegally, as Mr. Lazarevic just said, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Illegally, yes. That's right. I said illegally. Illegal possession of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, you testified two days ago that upon arrival at the SUP for your assignment, you were told that it was "crime prevention and finding out the perpetrators." You were aware, in April, May, June 1992, that Serb forces had armed themselves and taken control of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, in opposition to the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina. You didn't investigate the arming of the Serb forces or their insurrection or armed rebellion against the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina under the Penal Code you've just referred us to, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object. I believe that through this question, my colleague is misleading the witness. First, we are talking about Serbs armed themselves, and whether arming of Serbs, which by this moment we already know that was done through the JNA and in the period when the JNA existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to what my learned friend is saying in front of the witness on the record. There's a proper way of making an objection, and that's not the way to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And besides that, the question is clear. The witness can answer. So go ahead, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Sarkanovic, do you understand -- do you remember the question I just asked you or do you want me to repeat it? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: List the first part, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question was: Two days ago, you testified that upon arrival at the SUP for your assignment, you were told that it was crime prevention and your assignment was "crime prevention and finding out the perpetrators." You were aware in April, May, and June of 1992 that Serb forces had armed themselves and taken control of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, in opposition to the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, you didn't investigate the arming of the Serb forces or their insurrection or armed rebellion against the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina under the Penal Code referred to a few moments ago, did you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when I came to the SUP, and as I have already stated, in order to work on crime prevention and finding out the perpetrators of criminal offences, that was more or less the main duty of the crime department, which had done this work before and was supposed to continue doing it. And bearing in mind the situation that was in place at the time, which was that in the detention and the SUP premises and the TO premises, there were already people who were there, and I said that, first of all, we started to talk and take statements from the detainees regarding the circumstances of illegal arming and belonging to paramilitary units. As far as the Serbs were concerned, they were armed as members of the reserve force of the army, that is, at that time, of the legal units that were in the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, your testimony has been that Serb forces and -- Serb paramilitary forces and police had taken control of Bosanski Samac. Your evidence yesterday was that Serb forces and Serb authorities had displaced the democratically elected government and were controlling the municipality. A moment ago you told us that your mission was to investigate armed rebellion and insurrection. What I've just told you describes a state of armed rebellion and insurrection against the state, that is, Serb paramilitaries and police taking control of the organs of government and the facilities in a democratically elected institution. I repeat my question: You didn't investigate -- let me finish the question, please. You can object when I finish the question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I repeat my question: In the circumstances I've described, you did not investigate the arming of Serbs or their insurrection against the state in seizing control of a democratically elected municipality, did you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a position to work and to do what I wanted to do. I was doing what I was ordered to do, and I was ordered by the chief of the station, Stevan Todorovic, through my direct superior, Milos Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying you were prevented from carrying out your mission, which was to investigate armed rebellion and the insurrection that had actually occurred in Bosanski Samac by your superiors, Stevan Todorovic and Milos Savic? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I wish to say is I was doing what I was ordered to do, which was to interview and take statements from the detained persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your testimony two days ago was of your mission being to -- your assignment was "crime prevention and finding out the perpetrators." While you were working in the SUP for those two months, it was very obvious to you that very, very serious crimes had been committed and were being committed on a daily basis by Serb forces in Bosanski Samac, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's right. But I said that we wanted to conduct on-site investigations on certain sites of incidents and criminal offences, but Stevan Todorovic wouldn't let us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say you wanted to conduct on-site investigations, sir, you were actually working on site of one of the major crime scenes in Bosanski Samac, weren't you, the SUP, because that is where many of the daily beatings and torture of prisoners was occurring; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about it, and I also said that we were not allowed to do that. I said that these crimes took place, but I also said that we were not allowed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, also from my reading of the transcript, I wish to clarify -- I'd like you to assist the Trial Chamber by clarifying the lines of authority of the people who worked in interviewing people and the chain of command. If you could be provided --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wish to provide the witness with a piece of paper and ask him to draw a diagram, in which he places the names and positions of those working in the SUP between April and June 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You understand what I want you to do, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before you start drawing, I'm just holding up a piece of paper here, sir, Mr. Sarkanovic. I'm just holding up a piece of paper with boxes and lines on it. I have written nothing on it. I'd like you, if possible, to do it in that style: Boxes and lines; and if they go in two directions, please do it that way.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You have a box at the top of the page which is displayed on the monitor for us. What have you written there, please?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Chief."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please put the name of the chief, as well as the position -- put the names of the people, as well as their positions, perhaps in a different-coloured pen.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. In blue, you have the position chief in the top box and the name Stevan Todorovic. There's an arrow pointing down to the next box. Please read what that says.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Chief of the crime department, Milos Savic."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you have a line pointing to another box underneath that, and it says "inspector."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Inspector Vladimir Sarkanovic." That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please put the names of other people who were working as inspectors with you in that box.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no one else. When I left, then Simo Bozic came. But at the time when I was there, there was no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you for drawing that diagram for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can I have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be treated as P170 ter. Thank you. ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Sarkanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to ask the Prosecution to have it translated formally, the diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We will do that straight away, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Sarkanovic, yesterday I was asking you about the system of the establishment of detention centres. I just want to clarify something from yesterday. The prisoners at the SUP and the other detention facilities, who was feeding them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday, in response to a question from Mr. Pantelic, you said you interviewed between, you think, 50 to 100 people, while you were working at the SUP over that two-month period. I think you said there were people whose names appeared on lists. Over your career, you would have interviewed hundreds, probably thousands of people, during your career as a police inspector, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Inaudible]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think the witness said yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the usher please assist the witness to sit close to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can do it by myself. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And for you, of course, as a police inspector, the interviewing or taking statements is a routine part of your job, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And it's not a routine part of a person's life to be interrogated or interviewed by a police inspector, especially when in custody; you would agree with that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And for that reason, a person who is interviewed or interrogated is more likely to remember the specific details, the finer details of the interview, the questions, and the circumstances of it than the interviewer, who has performed hundreds or thousands of these interviews as part of his routine daily duties?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday I asked you about your interviewing of Mr. Tihic - I'm sorry - the interviewing of Mr. Tihic in the police station. I just want to clarify several things which were unclear from my reading of the transcript last night, Mr. Sarkanovic. Your evidence was that Mr. Zaric was the person who interviewed Mr. Tihic, but you also spoke to Mr. Tihic. That was your evidence, wasn't it? Just in summary.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said - and I stand by that - that the statement and the official part of the interview was conducted by Mr. Zaric. He's the one who took the statement. My involvement was more or less private, speaking to him as a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You spoke to Mr. Zaric after he had obtained the statement from Mr. Tihic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Tihic was brought to my office before Mr. Zaric came to the same office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, you had formed the view that there was no reason for Mr. Tihic to be in custody at that point, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: That was my private opinion. After the taking of the statement, the usual practice was that the statement would go to the chief, Stevan Todorovic, where elements of it would be assessed, on the basis of that statement. So all the -- whether there were elements that constituted criminal offence. And then that -- the proceedings would go further or people were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, your evidence on Monday - that's at page 16516 to 16517 of the transcript - was that when Mr. Tihic was at the police station, and you and Mr. Zaric were talking to him, your evidence was: "We encouraged Mr. Tihic. We told him that there was no reason for him to be further detained in the station after the interview. So in that sense, we told him that after the interview he would be released."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also said that I occasionally came in. I wasn't present throughout the interview. I occasionally came into the office. And it's true that I said that. That was before the statement was taken. And this was just me talking to him, as friend to a friend, because the entire official part regarding taking of the statement, that was done by Mr. Zaric. What I said, that was just me speaking as a friend to him, not knowing at all what Mr. Tihic would state. I was encouraging Mr. Tihic, and another time when we saw him, three or four days later [as interpreted], although I was not taking a statement from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, if you -- and your task was, you've already told us, to investigate --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I really don't want to interrupt, but the witness said: "When I saw him three or four days later," in page 12, line 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, your evidence two days ago - and I was reading directly from the transcript - was we, that is you and Mr. Zaric, encouraged him, we, you and Mr. Zaric, told him there was no reason for him to be further detained, and we, you and Mr. Zaric, told him after the interview that he would be released. Okay? Now, your mission, you've told us, or your assignment, was to investigate armed rebellion and illegal arming. Just let me finish the question, please. Armed rebellion or illegal arming. If there was evidence against Mr. Tihic of his involvement in the illegal arming or the armed rebellion which you were investigating, you would not have told him that he should be released from the police station, would you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: At that time, there was no proof. There was only suspicion that a crime had been committed. As for proof, there wasn't any. And the suspicion was based on the lists that were found in the premises or in the cupboard or the desk of the commander of the reserve force. I did not know what Mr. Tihic would say at the time, let alone whether a crime had actually been committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, if Mr. Tihic had confessed to leading an armed rebellion against the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina in his interview, you would not have told him that he would be released or should be released from custody, would you, because he would have been in the category of the person, the type of person you were interested in investigating and detaining for the commission of those offences?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for whether a crime had been committed or not, whether there were sufficient elements to prove that, that was not for me to say. It was up to the chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you spoke to Mr. Tihic and told him he should be released from detention, you were aware that he had not confessed to taking part in an armed rebellion or illegal arming, and Mr. Zaric was aware of that too, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you: Actually, I'm saying this yet again. This talk took place before the statement was actually taken. Until the present day, I haven't read that statement, because once it's taken, it was sent to Chief Todorovic. I do not know what Mr. Tihic actually stated at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, were you present when Mr. Zaric said to Mr. Tihic something to the effect of: If it was up to me - that's Simo Zaric - I'd release you, but I can't make such a decision without speaking to Blagoje Simic, and also without speaking to Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present. However, I heard that this interview did take place and that Mr. Zaric asked Mr. Todorovic for him to be released but that the other man refused it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you present when Mr. Zaric telephoned Mr. Blagoje Simic to discuss releasing Mr. Tihic from custody?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Zaric tell you about telephoning or speaking to Mr. Simic about releasing Mr. Tihic from custody?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say for sure whether it was Mr. Zaric, but that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've agreed earlier that the prisoner is more likely to remember the circumstances of the interrogation and interview than the interrogator. Mr. Tihic says that after the interview --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... not allowed in these proceedings to impeach the statement of one witness with another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not impeaching. He's already conceded that the interrogatee is more likely to remember the circumstances than the interrogator. I'm not impeaching the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. On this matter, the witness -- the Trial Chamber is of the view that the witnesses of the same party cannot be confronted during cross-examination by using the evidence of another witness as against another witness, of the same party. But the witnesses of an opposing party can be -- the evidence of witnesses of an opposing party can be put to the other -- to the witnesses of the opposing party. So the Prosecution can put the evidence of their witnesses to the evidence of the witnesses of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may repeat my objection for the record. This puts the Defence in a very unfair position toward Prosecution. They go with their case first, and their witnesses come one by one, and we cannot impeach them with our witnesses because we still do not have any witnesses in our case. So this puts us in a very unfair position towards Prosecution. We have nothing that we can present to their witnesses, because we don't have statements of our witnesses yet, in the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. That is not correct, because by the time the trial starts, the Defence will have already known what their defence is. So they would put those issues of their defence case to the witnesses of the Prosecution. So it's not a question of having formal statements before the Trial Chamber, no. It's a question of what the defence which the accused persons are putting up, and those are the issues that you use in cross-examining the Prosecution witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I say something? I have fully understood your decision, but I wish to recall the position of the Trial Chamber that if one witness is shown what another witness had said, this cannot undermine the latter witness's credibility. You said yourself that you can have questions reworded. Regardless of the side on which individual witnesses are, then in this way, the witness can be confused by the words of another witness. So words from the testimony of another witness cannot be taken from another testimony. It should not be done so directly. The other witness should not be quoted directly, because in this way, this witness is influenced by the words of another witness, the actual words. That was my interpretation of the original decision. A while ago, I was not allowed to put questions in relation to what a person said, and this person had not been a Prosecution witness. This is when I was putting questions to Mr. Kemal Mehinovic. I wanted to put questions to him related to police proceedings, and you would not allow me to do that. I understood your decision, but the question can simply be reworded, and it is then that the witness can say what he has to say in relation to such matters, because I think that in this way, we are being brought into a position of inequality.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I make it quite clear? I was not intending to confront the witness with Mr. Tihic's testimony. I'm not attempting to impeach this witness with another witness's testimony. That wasn't my intention. That's not what I'm attempting to do. There's no forensic purpose in me doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think let me explain. What the Prosecution can do is to paraphrase the questions and then put them to the -- the evidence, rather, and put that to the witness, instead of citing the actual evidence of the witness and naming the witness. Understood? For instance, you can say there is evidence before this Trial Chamber to the effect that... whatever the evidence is, and then you ask the witness what he says to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, there is evidence to the effect before this Trial Chamber that after you had this conversation with Mr. Tihic, he wasn't in fact released but was in fact taken back downstairs to a cell, one metre by twenty metres, approximately, in area, with seven to nine people in it, and remained incarcerated there until he was transferred elsewhere. You've got no reason to disagree with that, do you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he went there. However, I don't know how many people had already been there. That's the only thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is also evidence that before he was placed in the cell, either you or Mr. Zaric said that he couldn't be put together with other detainees in the headquarters of the Territorial Defence because he had gotten to know them already. Now, before you answer, I want to ask you something further, and that's this: If either you or Mr. Zaric said that to Mr. Todorovic, was it, in effect, a ruse when you said that to try and get him away from further beatings, to try and get him away from the spot where he was likely to be beaten further?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was the one who suggested that, for the following reason: So that he would not be sent to the TO, where the members of the special units would stop by, especially during the night, and beat up these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But what I'm asking is the way you phrased it when you said it to Mr. Todorovic, the way you put it, was to frame it by saying: This person, Tihic, shouldn't be put together with those other detainees because he already knows who they are, in an attempt to fool Mr. Todorovic into putting Mr. Tihic somewhere else, or persuade, if "fool" is the wrong word.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not say that to Mr. Stevan Todorovic at all. This was a conversation between Mr. Zaric, Mr. Milos Savic, and myself. Stevan Todorovic was not present at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric also agreed that Mr. Tihic should be released from custody, and you said you had heard that he had spoken to Mr. Simic about that. Now, Mr. Zaric's view on Mr. Tihic was that he should be released because there was no evidence against him, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had heard --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One small clarification. I really don't feel like interrupting my colleague, but that he had spoken, that you heard that he had spoken to Mr. Simic. The witness said he didn't hear exactly that Mr. Zaric talked to Mr. Simic but that he heard about the two of them were talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If you check line 22 of the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a matter of phrasing, because what we heard as translation is that: You heard that Mr. Zaric was -- it's a bit hard to explain. It's our language. It suggests that he was present when Mr. Zaric was speaking to Mr. Simic. That's the only reason. And we understood that perfectly. But in our language, it sounded that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we can just repeat the question, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Sarkanovic, a moment ago I asked you -- I'm going to repeat the question slowly: Mr. Zaric agreed with you that Mr. Simic - sorry - that Mr. Tihic should be released from custody, and you told us, not long ago, that you had heard that he, Mr. Zaric, you weren't present, but you had heard that he, Mr. Zaric, had spoken to Mr. Simic about that, that's Tihic's release - let me finish, please. Now, Mr. Zaric's view about Mr. Tihic's detention was that he should be released because there was no evidence against him, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say this once again. The conversation about this took place before Mr. Zaric conducted the official interview with Mr. Tihic. After that, I heard - and actually, at that time we thought about this - afterwards, I heard that Mr. Zaric had called Mr. Blagoje Simic in relation to the release of Mr. Tihic. I don't know how all of this ended, but Tihic was not released.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You heard that Mr. Simic and Mr. Zaric had spoken after the interview had occurred, didn't you, not before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard indirectly. I was not there. I said it, and I'm saying it now: I was not present, but I heard that they had talked. I heard indirectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, that wasn't my question. My question was when. You heard after the interview. It was after the interview had occurred that you heard that Mr. Zaric and Mr. Simic had spoken - let me finish, please - had spoken about Mr. Tihic's release, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the interview. After the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you know the reason why Mr. Zaric spoke to Mr. Simic about that was because Mr. Zaric believed or knew there was no evidence justifying Mr. Tihic's continued detention?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Calling for speculation.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the reason why Mr. Zaric spoke --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Surely it must be within the witness -- and the witness can answer whether he knows or not. I mean, I don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please, and can you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question was: You know the reason why Mr. Zaric spoke to Mr. Simic about Mr. Tihic's release was because Mr. Zaric believed or knew, when he spoke to Mr. Simic, that there was no evidence justifying Mr. Tihic's continued detention?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just assume why Mr. Zaric called Mr. Simic, but Mr. Zaric was not in a position to assess Mr. Tihic's statement as to whether a crime had been committed or not been committed, because this is a right that only Stevan Todorovic had. Though Simo could only present his own view, his personal view.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That, of itself, Mr. Zaric's -- I withdraw that. Mr. Zaric, as far as you know, didn't telephone Mr. Simic asking for the release of 50 to 100 people who you had interviewed in suspicion of conducting an armed rebellion for illegally arming themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about 20th of April in relation to Mr. Tihic at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've moved on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At that point there is no evidence that there was 100 or 150 [sic] people arrested at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've moved on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question is: As far as you know, Mr. Zaric didn't telephone Mr. Simic in relation to the release or asking for the release of the 50 to 100 people that you say you interviewed over that two-month period, and you interviewed them in suspicion of conducting -- with suspicion of conducting an armed rebellion or illegally arming themselves. As far as you know, Mr. Zaric didn't ring or speak to Mr. Simic asking for their release, did he?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the transfer of prisoners from the TO building, I have already said that the following day, after the detainees had been transferred, I heard that they had been transferred from the TO for their own security and safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, my question was their release. Your evidence is that you had heard Mr. Zaric telephoned -- had heard that he had telephoned Mr. Simic asking for Mr. Tihic's release, that is his freedom, and you had told Mr. Tihic he should be free to leave. As far as you know, Mr. Zaric did not telephone, make the same telephone calls to Mr. Blagoje Simic in relation to the 50 to 100 people you interviewed on suspicion of illegally arming or conducting an armed rebellion?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he did that or not, whether he telephoned or not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The fact that he had telephoned Mr. Simic in relation to Mr. Tihic's release from custody, and you're unaware of him telephoning in relation to all the other people in custody strongly suggests that he believed that Mr. Tihic was innocent, after taking the interview, and that there was no legitimate reason for his continued detention, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only engage in guesswork. How can I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, in the circumstances I've just outlined, you know he telephoned or you heard he telephoned in relation to one prominent person after interviewing him, seeking his release, but not all the others. The fact that he telephoned in relation to one person and went straight to the top, that's the head of the Crisis Staff, suggests that he believed that person was innocent or there was no evidence justifying his detention. That's the only conclusion you, as a police inspector, with a law degree, can draw from those actions, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've just said: I can give my opinion, but it is not relevant at all. If you want me to do that, I shall. The assumption is fine, but I don't know whether that's actually what happened. The assumption is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The assumption being fine, sir, yesterday Mr. Lazarevic showed you two documents: D14/4 and D25/4. Those were the lists -- the SDA lists containing all the names. You remember seeing those documents? Yes?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic's name appeared on those documents, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the fact that Mr. Zaric was importuning Mr. Simic for the release of this person who - and you agreed with the assumption or the conclusion that he must have believed he was innocent or there was no evidence if he went to the step of asking the head of the Crisis Staff to release him - casts real doubts upon the authenticity of those documents, if Mr. Zaric took that step, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object to this question. This is call for speculation 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday the witness was asked to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How could the witness know what Mr. Zaric had at this moment. Mr. Zaric could also have some other assumptions. I can say that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm happy to break the question down into three, but yesterday my learned friend Mr. Lazarevic specifically asked the witness to authenticate the document and the witness gave an explanation of what he thought the document contained. My questioning is just a logical a contrario argument, I suppose. But if it assists, I can certainly break the question down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You break it down so the question can understand each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Sarkanovic, agreeing with the assumption that the only reason you agreed with that assumption that Mr. Zaric would have rung Mr. Simic was because he would have believed that, after interviewing Mr. Tihic, there was no basis to keep him in custody. The fact that Mr. Tihic's name appeared on those documents and Mr. Zaric was importuning the president of the Crisis Staff for his release must, in your mind, as a police inspector with a law degree, cast some doubts on the authenticity, at least in part, of those two documents, mustn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If my colleague can explain what is the difference of this question between the previous one. It's exactly the same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you understand the question, Mr. Sarkanovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... can you please answer it, then.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: 90 per cent of detainees that I interviewed, they refused to say that they had been members of paramilitary units, that they were in any way linked to this, although, on the basis of some other statements where cooperation was somewhat different. I don't know how many, 100, 200 pieces of weapons were taken away. Even those who said that they didn't participate, they did, and they had weapons found. So obviously, I would allow for the possibility that on the list, there were persons who were not connected to this. However, a large number of persons had been involved in the units and in the arming.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Tihic's name featured prominently on both lists. Zaric telephoned Simic asking for Tihic's release after interviewing.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That of itself must in your mind have cast some doubts on the list's authenticity, at least as it involved Mr. Tihic's name being on it, mustn't it? Just confine yourself to Tihic's name being on the list.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you: I don't know what you want me to say. I have already stated what I think. I can assume what you're saying is that Mr. Zaric had this in mind when he made that call, but I don't know that. He didn't tell me that. I can assume that, just like you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, the fact that he telephoned Simic, asking for Zaric's release of a man whose name featured prominently on the list, which you were using to conduct your investigations must, in your mind, I suggest, have cast some doubts on the authenticity of the document you were using, at least insofar as Mr. Tihic's name was on it, although not necessarily the other names. You must agree with that, mustn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not insofar as I'm concerned. If you're thinking about the authenticity of the list and everything else, no, because these lists had been proven authentic before. But I told you already that there were people who had said and for whom it had been proved that they were not members of the units and they had not been armed and they had not had weapons found with them. There were cases. That's what I said. But there was no doubt as to the authenticity of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Re, can we move on? We've been on this point for too long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Re, I'd just like to pose one short question before you do that, to Mr. Sarkanovic. Do you know whether Mr. Zaric released himself any other detainees without speaking to Dr. Simic or to Mr. Todorovic? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he couldn't have done it, even theoretically. Only Stiv who could have done that. I don't know of that, in any case. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Do you recall two detainees, the surname of one was Mr. Jusufovic, and the other is a Mr. Fadil Sabanovic? Do those names mean anything to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fadil Sabanovic and Jusufovic, yes. He was the son of the cake shop owner, Ferid. Yes. At the time when Mr. Zaric was speaking to Mr. Tihic, I think I was interviewing with one, and then the other, in an office which is used as a conference hall. We saw that yesterday, that is, the room which is opposite my office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And were these two gentlemen released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard later that they were released. I don't know who released them, but only Stiv could have released them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Sarkanovic, Dragan Lukac, your former colleague, was arrested on the 17th of April, 1992 and detained, and while in custody, was severely beaten by one of the paramilitaries, Lugar. You accept that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was severely beaten up, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you interviewed him after he had been severely beaten by Lugar, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when Lugar had beaten him up, but I know that when I spoke to him, he still bore traces of the beating. I don't know whether Lugar was responsible or someone else, but there were traces that were visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic [sic] - don't get me wrong in any way - said your treatment of him was fair and proper, but you, of course, because of all the large number of statements you took, you can't remember the details -- I just want to clarify something for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] For the transcript. You are using the word Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel please. Microphone. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. You're using the word "Lukic." This is the name of the counsel, not of the witness. And again, we have instructions from the Trial Chamber not to challenge the testimony of this witness. So you can say: We have evidence in this case. Not: Mr. Lukac said in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The second that was drawn to my attention, I was attempting to correct it, which I will now continue to try to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Sarkanovic, I'm clearly referring to Dragan Lukac, not Novak Lukic, seated over there. My question is - I've told you he has told that there's evidence that your treatment of him was fair and proper - that my question is: You've already agreed that you would not be able to remember the details of someone's interrogation more than the person who is interrogated. Mr. Lukac described his state at the time of his interview by you, which he said was fair and proper, as being in a state of psychological shock. You can't disagree with his assessment of his own position when you interviewed him as being in a state of psychological shock, can you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is quite possible. I agree with that, because he was really in a very poor condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And there's evidence before this Trial Chamber that in view of the state that he was in, he couldn't say whether the statement he gave was complete or whether it was recorded faithfully, or whether it was all in there, that is, whether everything that he said was recorded in the statement?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: Regardless of the condition that Mr. Lukac was in, I allowed him to -- made it possible for him as a colleague that after the interview that we had, that he himself, by himself, would dictate this statement to be recorded as his statement. This statement that you probably have has been dictated by Dragan Lukac, regardless of his condition, of the condition that he was in. If he had not done it -- if he had done it incorrectly, I followed it while he was dictating. More or less we knew what we were talking about, what was supposed to go into the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Lukac, having experienced -- having been beaten and having experienced severe psychological shock, was really in no position to give an accurate, reliable, and completely voluntary statement, no matter how fair or proper you were of him during your interview with him; you would agree with that, wouldn't you, because that would be consistent with what you told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: I probably said that yesterday. I'm going to say it again. Any detainee that I spoke to, whether it was Lukac or someone else, was asked if he wanted to give a statement. Nobody - and if this is different, then show me the statement -- but nobody was forced to give a statement, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you should be winding up now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I am winding up. I was only asking about Dragan Lukac not the other people and I'm asking the witness to concentrate only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's not the point. I'm simply telling you you should be winding up now. You have had three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I am winding up. I'm almost there. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Look, Mr. Sarkanovic, I was only asking you about Dragan Lukac. You're saying that he was in the same category as the other detainees who were beaten and experiencing severe psychological shock and that any statement he gave, no matter how professional or gentle you were --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Inaudible]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There was something we said we didn't catch, but I'll finish my question. No matter how professional or gentle you were in your interviewing of him, because of the circumstances of its taking, it would of its very nature be unreliable?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The actual statement is not regarded as evidence in the proceedings. It can be changed several times, completely. So the statement that is given during the interview, interviewed by an inspector, by me, does not represent any kind of evidence. So he could have said all kinds of things, and then he could have just denied it afterwards? You understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the crime that Dragan Lukac had committed that justified his arrest on the 17th of April, 1992, and his incarceration - just let me finish before you answer, please. I know you want to answer it, but please - and his exchange on the 4th of September, 1992? What was his crime?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the suspicion while he was detained, but the criminal offence, I didn't assess that, or I didn't assess of any of the other detainees that I spoke to. So the assessment whether there was a criminal offence that was committed, that was ruled on by Stevan Todorovic, and only by Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said yesterday that Mr. Zaric had only taken one statement. For time purposes, I'm not going to show you his record of interview, but in his record of interview or statement to the Prosecutor, that's P141, at page 5, I think, he said he had actually taken at least four. You can't disagree with that, because you didn't see him take these interviews; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you: I only saw one, but he could have taken not four, he could have taken 14 and I wouldn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I only wanted to clarify your evidence yesterday when you said he only took one, and we clarified it that he only took one that you know of; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I knew, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sir, finally, I'll finish now. I've already asked you about the very serious crimes that you were aware of that had been committed by the Serb forces, the police, the paramilitary, Mr. Todorovic, and those who had ordered the arrests and detention of people on ethnic grounds. You said yesterday that this system horrified you and you didn't want to take any part of it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Inaudible]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The answer is not picked up by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We didn't hear what you said. Can you just lean closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said -- perhaps I said it very quietly, but here I am quite close.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We were actually interested in what you said. What was your answer.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, yes I said it. What the Prosecutor said. I said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Sarkanovic, in normal circumstances, if those things -- if you had witnessed or were aware of those horrific crimes being committed, you would have taken action or complained to someone to institute action against -- criminal proceedings against those responsible for those crimes, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you tell me who, then that would be an affirmative answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If those things had happened when you were working as a police inspector before the war, that the police in charge of -- the police officer in charge of the station was beating and torturing detainees, you would have made a complaint up the line, wouldn't you, or asked someone to investigate this gross abuse of authority? I'm talking before the war. That's what you would have done, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object. Here, the witness is being presented with a hypothetical situation: What would have been had this happened, in normal circumstances. So this is a hypothetical question, an "if" clause. What would the witness then in a situation if something had been the case. Now, when the Defence was asking questions in this way, the Trial Chamber said the Defence did not have the right to ask questions of witnesses in this way, so we think that this way of asking questions is not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re. The objection is sustained. You are asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not asking the witness to speculate. I'm asking him on procedures. It's specifically on complaints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But you are telling him that if it had happened this way, what would you have done, or you would have done it this or that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the man spent 18 years as police inspector presumably during that time he would have seen some instances of police abuse. It happens in every system in the world. There would have been systems in place as to what to do. It's part of your training, it's part of police regulations, as far as I know, everywhere in the world, what to do if a crime occurs in the police station. All I'm asking him is: Before the war, this is what you would have done, and I'm just about to move to the next thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It is still asking him to speculate if the things had been the way you are putting it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Sarkanovic, during your time as a police inspector, did you ever make complaints about or did you ever witness offences committed by police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see it, but there was no need for me to complain to anyone. We would do our work and we were not prevented in doing it by someone. We would have done it had we not been prevented from doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm only asking you about the situation before and during the war. Before the war, had a murder occurred in the police station, as a police officer, it would have been investigated and a complaint would have been made; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Sarkanovic. Again, there is a question with an "if" clause. Again, had there been a murder before the war, and to make a parallel. But first of all, this witness is a fact witness, not an expert witness, and certainly not a witness regarding the assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness has already answered. He said: I've answered it, I think meaning, naturally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You should be asking him. Obviously, crimes did occur before the war, so you ask him if anything had occurred before the war, what the witness did, or what the police officers did in those situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If murders occurred in police stations -- when murders occurred --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. When murders occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When beatings occurred in police stations, and I assume they occasionally did, as in most systems, it has occurred, and it shouldn't, there were systems in place before the war for reporting or investigating police misconduct in -- well, in an official capacity, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was a transgression in terms of use of force, there would either be disciplined procedure or a criminal procedure -- criminal proceedings, depending on what kind of transgression it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But of course what you saw in the police station during the war, that's April, May, June 1992, went far beyond the use of excessive force, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've already us that it was -- what you saw horrified you. But what also horrified you was that there was nothing you could do about it, that there was no one you could complain to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we were prevented from doing such work. There were people we could have reported this to. There was the prosecutor's office and so on. But we were banned. We were forbidden from doing this at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you were horrified that any complaint you would have made would have gone back to those responsible for implementing this system in Bosanski Samac in 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the assessment regarding whether there was a criminal offence committed or not, this was decided on by the chief of the station, Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Re, that's over.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just ask one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Your time is over.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just on Todorovic, one issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I told you to wind up. I've allowed you to go on for 10, 15 minutes --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just one issue in relation to Todorovic, which should be about two questions, Your Honour. That's all I ask for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Todorovic was, of course, a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume he was, yes. Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the SDS -- sorry - and Blagoje Simic and the Crisis Staff -- sorry - the Crisis Staff was controlled by the SDS?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And a complaint to Todorovic would have gone to the SDS about what you saw in the police station, and you were afraid that nothing would come of any complaint you made because of Todorovic's position; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Re. The witness already said he didn't know, so you can't build on that and ask the question you have asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He said that Todorovic was a member of the SDS. He said: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But the latter part that the Crisis Staff was controlled by the SDS, he said he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He said I assume so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He can only assume so, which doesn't take us anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. I'd actually like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, before you start, the Judge would like to ask a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'd actually like the assistance of our registry assistant to show two exhibits to the witness, and I would like the witness simply to look at the signatures and see if he can identify the signatures. The first is Exhibit D28/3, and the second one is the immediately following exhibit, D29/3. Obviously, to give the witness the ter document in both cases. So, Mr. Sarkanovic, if you could just look at the signatures and comment on the signature on the right in each case. There's a signature on the left and then there's a signature on the right. It's the one on the right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the right-hand side is my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. That is D28/3 ter, the first document? Yes? And then the second document, if you could just do the same thing, 29/3 ter, signature on the right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is Milos Savic's signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is. I think I said in the reserve, but I believe it is his.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And just before we break, just one other short question. I believe it was Mr. Krgovic yesterday or the day before raised the issue of blank pages with signatures on, in terms of detainees giving interviews, and I just wanted to be clear. Did you, with any of the persons that you interviewed in the SUP during this period, April 1992 to June, did you ever ask any of the persons you interviewed to sign a blank sheet of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never. Each person I interviewed could have refused to sign his own statement that he had already stated. I don't know what I -- what use would I have had blank piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And one last question: Did you know or did you hear whether other persons, including some of the specials, the paramilitaries, such as Lugar and Crni and so on, did they ever make persons sign a blank sheet of paper? Detained persons, obviously.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't heard that they had forced them. Perhaps they would have taken money from them. But no. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll take our break and continue our proceedings at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Sarkanovic. In order to clarify matters, because I didn't want to keep objecting while my colleague the Prosecutor was conducting his cross-examination: Whenever you answered him in the following terms: "I think," "I assume," et cetera, does that mean that you were not 100 per cent sure and that you can only guess [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Instead of -- just correction to the transcript. I asked him in B/C/S language, instead of word "guess" it should be speculate. Thank you. Just for the correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Sarkanovic: When my colleague the Prosecutor asked you about the episode related to the telephone conversation between Mr. Zaric and Mr. Blagoje Simic, did you find out later on or did you hear that on that occasion Dr. Blagoje Simic said to Zaric that the subject-matter related to the release of Tihic was not within Blagoje Simic's jurisdiction; it was within the line of work of Stevan Todorovic, chief of police, and that he, as an employee, should sort it out with him? Did you hear that later?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was exactly that way, but it was along those lines, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There is something in this question that it's not quite clear to me, that -- he said: As an employee, did Mr. Pantelic refer that Mr. Zaric was an employee of Mr. Todorovic? Because frankly, I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic can clear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I can rephrase, yes. I can rephrase. I can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Sarkanovic, the point is in the following: You heard later that Blagoje Simic had said that this was not within his jurisdiction but that this was within the line of work of the police, of the police authorities, Stevan Todorovic. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether that's exactly what I said, but it was along those lines, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, the Prosecutor asked you about some crimes, namely, armed rebellion against a certain state, et cetera, and you said that the state concerned was Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, I am asking you the following: During that period while you worked as a police inspector, was there an entity called Republika Srpska, or rather, the Republic of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about the fact that at that time there was a constitution of Republika Srpska and certain laws?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at least I'm not aware of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at that time, there was a Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska, that is to say, the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During the cross-examination of my learned friend Mr. Re, he put a series of questions to you, starting between the 16th and 17th of April, when the armed conflicts in Samac started, slowly but surely, he led you to some answers that are not quite clear. I would like to clarify them now. He mentioned, on page 51 of yesterday's transcript - it was line 9 - he spoke about the new system that was established and that ordered or allowed mass arrests, et cetera. As regards this term "new system," do you mean the municipal authorities, the Crisis Staff, or Stevan Todorovic and the specials? What is your understanding of this new system or new regime?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan Todorovic and the specials.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, on page 50 of the transcript, yesterday's transcript, I mean, line 3 and 4, and again, there is your answer, he asked you whether the municipal authorities are responsible for the safety of the population and the property security of the population, and your answer was yes. And now I'm asking you, as an experienced policeman, whether the local police is under the control of the local authorities or the appropriate authorities within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The appropriate authorities within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In conclusion, in relation to Stevan Todorovic, first and foremost, Mr. Sarkanovic, did you ever attend in any official capacity meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I was not a member of the Crisis Staff and there was no need [Realtime transcript read in error "was need"] for me to attend these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How would you describe Stevan Todorovic? After all, he was a layman in police work. Did he boast --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The answer that the witness gave was not properly recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On page 41, line 19: I was not a member of the Crisis Staff and there was no need for me. There is "no" missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Sarkanovic, how would you describe Stevan Todorovic? What category would you place him in? Was he a professional in his work? Was he a calm person, a cultured person, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I withdraw, I withdraw, I withdraw. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Sarkanovic: Do you know, with absolute certainty, that he was a member of the Crisis Staff, on the basis of some decisions, on the basis of some proclamations, some official document, or did he tell you that, or rather, did you just assume that? On the basis of what did you answer the Prosecutor along those lines that you knew that he was a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Any objection I was going to make, I withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The question was clear for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've finished with my re-examination. [Interpretation] That you, Mr. Sarkanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any questions, Mr. Lukic, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon once again, Mr. Sarkanovic. I would just like to clarify a few matters now that arose during the cross-examination, so could you please give me some clarifications in terms of the questions that were put to you and the answers that you gave. First of all, this last matter, Mr. Pantelic's question. So in order to clarify this fully: Was Mr. Zaric an employee of the MUP, or rather, of the secretariat of the interior of the public security station, and was Todorovic his superior?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown document D28/3 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you've seen this document. It was shown to you. Judge Williams already asked you to identify the signatures. Could you please put it there on the overhead projector next to you. Sir, the second sentence of the statement that starts: "During the night between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992," can you read that? Read it to yourself. There is no need to read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Underneath statement, there is a sentence, the first one, that says "unable to," and the other one that starts with "between the 16th and 17th of April, during the night." Could you just read it to yourself. And please go on to read the next sentence immediately, that is "in the morning, when gunshots were heard."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I just have a few questions to put to you in relation to that. During your testimony, during your testimony, you said that you personally saw, with your very own eyes, Esad Dagovic with a group of armed men, armed, in the morning, on the 17th, before your house. Is that what you stated before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm objecting. Can the witness please not answer the question. He knows not to answer if I'm objecting. The first point -- that's why I didn't interrupt you when you were -- I allowed you to make your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What is your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The objection is it doesn't arise from cross-examination. Her Honour Judge Williams asked a question about the signature on the bottom of the document. I asked the witness no questions at all relating to Esad Dagovic. There is nothing that arises, nor requires clarification, in my submission, from Her Honour Judge Williams's question about whose signature is on the bottom of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I may answer that. My colleague is completely right. He didn't ask specifically about Esad Dagovic, but all questions -- there was quite a number of questions related to the taking of statements, to the content of statements, whether they were properly taken, and the condition in which these statements were taken. What I'm trying to show with this, I believe that is quite obvious to the Trial Chamber and also to the Prosecution, that whatever conditions were, the statements are truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, if my learned friend is permitted to ask questions about Mr. Dagovic's incarceration and interrogation, I should be permitted to cross-examine the witness on that very point. I have questions prepared which I didn't go to on that point. Mr. Dagovic gave extensive testimony on that. I didn't take the witness to it. Either it doesn't arise or I should be allowed to re-cross, if he is allowed to ask those questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, you can go ahead and ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will allow the Prosecution to ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, it says here in this statement - I don't want to waste much time by reading it - it says here that he spent that night in his house and he was there with his brother and parents and neighbours in the basement of his house the following day. Is that what it says there? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And in this statement, it doesn't say anywhere here that he had weapons.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Has this statement also been compiled on the basis of what he told you during the interview?
