utterances.text: On this document, in the upper left-hand corner, one cannot see the corner, so I used the date from the other one where you could see the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell us: What date is this?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: The 1st of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The 1st of March. Did all members of the 4th Detachment have to have such permits, as well as members of other detachments that were within the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Everybody had to have this kind of permit and to carry them on their person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could anybody, especially you, as commander of the 4th Detachment, could you give permission to any member of the 4th Detachment to carry this kind of weaponry?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: All permits went from the Tactical Group, the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, now give me an answer to the following question: What about communications, communications equipment? What did the 4th Detachment have?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: I'm not a signalsman by training. I'm an infantryman. But I know what communications equipment is, the communications equipment used in the Yugoslav People's Army. These are field telephones, then an RUP 4, RUP 2, et cetera, other radio communications equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What equipment did you have at the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: An RUP 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this a radio transmitter?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is a radio transmitter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you remember where and when the members of the 4th Detachment were actually issued with this weapons and equipment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: The members of the 4th Detachment were issued weapons, quartermaster's equipment, and protection masks on two occasions. The first time this occurred at the training grounds that I already referred to, in Potocari, where there was an all-day training course for the members, and it is then that they were issued weapons and quartermaster's equipment. The second time was at the command of the 4th Detachment, and it concerned the weaponry that the 17th Tactical Group brought to the command in their own vehicles, so that people would not have to go individually to have all of this issued to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Did you monitor how these weapons were kept and how the members of the 4th Detachment behaved?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. The members of the 4th Detachment kept these weapons at their homes, but they were duty-bound to clean them, lubricate them, look at them, and if there was anything wrong, they were duty-bound to report this to the command so that the technical group could deal with this, either replace the weapon or repair it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Were there cases when members of the detachment used the weapons in contravention of the orders that you issued to them?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: No, not a single member could take weapons out into the street or show them in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now we're going to talk about the members of the 4th Detachment a bit. What was the life of the 4th Detachment like? Did they live in barracks? Was it that type of living, or was it somewhat different? What did they do? Could you just give us a brief description. And did they get any compensation for the fact that they belonged to the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: The members of the 4th Detachment were people with different professions. Many of them worked in certain companies. There were even some who had privately owned shops of their own in Samac and who were involved in certain crafts, arts, et cetera. Then there were some of us who were pensioners. So mostly people had their own jobs, and therefore, they did not receive any compensation from the Yugoslav People's Army, because it would have been senseless to employ these people and to give them compensation. So no compensation was given to people on account of the fact that they belonged to the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did the members of the 4th Detachment have to ask for permission to go away for a few days to finish some job? Did they have to ask the commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: No. The members of the 4th Detachment did not have to ask for permission. They were free men who could go around wherever they wanted to go, and so on. So no special permission was required in terms of their movement. They led normal lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: How did the command function? Did you have people on duty? How did you communicate with the command of the 17th Tactical Group? What did this look like?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: As for the command of the 17th Tactical Group, we most often communicated with them by telephone, so we talked. However, if it would happen that there was no electricity, for instance, then we used the communications equipment we were given through the establishment itself, because I had two signalsmen in the detachment, that is to say, two persons who were trained to use this kind of equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, if you remember, whether the existence of the 4th Detachment was a matter of public knowledge? Was this a secret organisation? What did this look like in public? In Bosanski Samac, did people know about this? Did the citizens know about this? Did you appear in the media? If so, tell us where and when? Could you tell us about this, about how you operated at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: When the 4th Detachment was established, the command immediately came to the conclusion that they should come out as an established unit of the Yugoslav People's Army. In that sense, we did come out. We were on the radio. We explained, particularly Mr. Zaric and I - Mr. Zaric in terms of the position he held and I as commander - we explained the reasons and the objectives why the 4th Detachment was established in the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was this within the programme of the radio station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. We expressed ourselves in writing as well, but the two of us were directly broadcast over Radio Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was this a live broadcast? Could the listeners put questions to you and so on?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember whether this was possible. I think that on one occasion the listeners could put questions. And on one occasion -- or the first time, rather, I remember that we explained the reasons why the 4th Detachment was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please, could you try to remember: How did you then explain through the media the objectives and tasks of the 4th Detachment of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: In that respect, that is to say, in terms of explaining the objectives, we asked the citizens to join us, the more the better. We asked them to look upon the 4th Detachment as a unit of their own. We explained that we were a mixed unit, that our joint objective was to spare Samac any kind of destruction, or rather, war operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you speak to the citizens then in favour of coexistence, tolerance, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the main motto of what we were saying. We were trying to spare the city of any destruction. We were calling for coexistence, togetherness. We were asking the citizens not to be divided along ethnic lines and other lines, and I think that we were rather successful in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the time has come for us to adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But before we do, I would like to ask the Prosecution to indicate their position on these statements: D45/4, 46/4, and 47/4, by Wednesday, next week, the 19th of March. Yes. We'll adjourn now and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 14th day of March 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
